messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING oncall: Elevated 5xx rate observed from eu-west-1 after a region rollout started ~02:05 UTC. Pager: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD-8721 — auto-created channel #incidents. Root alert: 5xx spike (api-proxy)
Jia: I got paged. jumping in now. any customer-facing reports?
SupportBot: Customer ticket #C-5542 reports timeouts from EU users since ~02:04 UTC. Affected customers: 3 tenants, increased latency for image-generation flows.
Sam: Confirming — logs show a surge of 502/504 from proxy -> runtime-v2-eu pods after traffic shift to green. Canary weight was bumped to 30% at 02:02 UTC.
Mika: Looking at pod logs, seen repeated KV cache misses and model-serving timeouts (rpc timeout). snippet: ```2026-03-11T02:03:12Z ERROR runtime-serving: kv-get timeout key=session:abc123```
Anya: Is this the new runtime build (v2) that was part of the green deployment?
Sam: Yes — green = runtime-v2 + new prefix caching enabled. Blue was runtime-v1.
Jia: Immediate plan: reduce traffic to green to 0% and set feature flag new-runtime-eu = off. Who can flip the flag?
Luis: I can toggle the FF via admin-console. Doing now. admin-api call: ```POST /flags/new-runtime-eu {"value": false, "env": "eu-west-1"}```
Luis: Flag flipped to false at 02:07:34 UTC. Rolling traffic back to blue via LB weight rollback (override applied).
oncall-sre: Applied region override: green weight -> 0, blue -> 100 at 02:07:50 UTC. Route change confirmed by edge metrics.
Mika: After rollback, 5xx rate dropping in eu-west-1. Current 5xx: was 18% at peak, now ~1.2% and falling.
Jia: Good. Is there any customer session/state loss? need to notify support/CS.
SupportBot: Support update posted to #support: "Mitigated: traffic rollback to stable runtime; investigating root cause. Customers may have seen transient errors between 02:02-02:08 UTC."
Sam: Initial hypothesis: runtime-v2 introduced aggressive prefix eviction which, combined with cross-region cold caches, produced KV misses and overloaded backends. Workload had many long-tail sequences from those three tenants.
Mika: Reproduced locally with a short test: enabling prefix-cache + concurrent requests shows kv-get latency spike when cache thrash occurs. Will capture traces.
Jia: Escalating to infra/research for a deeper root cause. Assigning: Mika (repro/trace), Sam (rollback/rollforward plan), Anya (customer comms).
Anya: Drafting customer impact note. Preliminary numbers: ~2.1k failed requests across affected tenants, approx 0.06% of global traffic. Potential SLO risk for those tenants — marking for postmortem.
Luis: Notes on DNS/region routing: DNS TTL for eu-edge is 60s; route change propagated fine. No DNS misrouting observed. This looks runtime-specific.
Sam: Next steps: pin green rollout in eu to disabled until we fix caching logic. We'll run a targeted canary in a sandbox with synthetic load and increased KV capacity.
Mika: Uploading traces and a minimal repro to the incident doc: https://redwood-internal/incident/1734567890/logs. also adding flamegraphs.
Jia: Oncall handoff: I'm staying until RCA action items are defined. If anyone else needs to take over, ping.
SupportBot: Customer-facing update scheduled in 30m with current mitigation and ETA for RCA.
Anya: Adding to postmortem: timeline, number of affected requests, feature-flag toggle time, LB rollback time, root-cause hypothesis, planned fix and verification steps.
Sam: Afterroot plan: revert aggressive eviction, add KV metrics/alerts (hot-key detection), and add a canary profile test for long-tail sequence workloads before future rollouts.
Jia: Marking incident status: mitigated. Closing active paging; follow-ups tracked in postmortem. :white_check_mark: 
incident-bot: Incident PD-8721 updated: status -> mitigated at 02:13:00 UTC.
Anya: Final note — support asked we proactively reach out to the three affected tenants with an apology and a summary of what happened. Assigning to CS to coordinate.
